newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani province bans fireworks after explosion.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani province bans fireworks after explosion.

text.p: The government of Pakistan's Sindh province banned fireworks on Sunday, a day after a store of firecrackers blew up, killing two people, wounding 19 and damaging six houses in the southern port city of Karachi.

The two-month ban on fireworks and the storage of explosive materials was imposed after Saturday's blast, which Deputy Inspector General of Police Malik Iqbal said had been caused by exploding firecrackers, not by a bomb as earlier thought.

He told a news conference firecrackers weighing a total of 40 kg (88 pounds) had blown up in the Saudabad area of District East. Another 43,344 Indian-made firecrackers, weighing 75 kg (165 pounds), had been recovered from a nearby house.
Iqbal said police were looking for the owner, identified only as Rajan, of the house where the explosion took place.
